newsitem.title: UK: Sad but proud, Thatcher bids farewell to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Sad but proud, Thatcher bids farewell to Hong Kong.

text.p: Former prime minister Margaret Thatcher said on Monday she felt both sad and proud that Britain was handing Hong Kong back to China after 156 years of colonial rule.

"I hope the world recognises what Britain and everything we stand for has done for Hong Kong. This enormous prosperity -- those six and a half million people who built it under British administration -- is a great achievement," Thatcher, who signed the 1984 Joint Declaration with China in 1984 on the handover, told BBC radio in Hong Kong.
Asked how she felt as the last hours of British rule ticked away, the Iron Lady said: "Very sad -- tinged with pride."
Britain had turned a piece of barren land into one of the world's top trading centres with income per head greater than that in Britain, Thatcher said.

"This could not have been done without that magical combination of the great talent and ability of Chinese people, and tremendous hard work, coupled with British rule of law, British administration and a sense of equity and fair play.

"Oh yes, show Hong Kong to the world and say: it's a combination of the Chinese personality and British administration, and let us take pride that we've brought this kind of success both economically and in freedom to this part of Asia," Thatcher said.
Thatcher was forced to stand down as prime minister and leader of the Conservative Party in 1990 by a party coup. She now sits in the upper House of Lords.
